record.title: Meta paper reports agentic experiment controls caught a false negative in a 37-day retrieval campaign
record.summary: Meta authors describe EvoPilot, a human-gated agent workflow for experiments spanning asynchronous training, publishing, serving and evaluation systems. In one 37-day Video Deep Dive campaign, an initial autoresearch comparison appeared to show a 22-point offline hit-rate decline, but review found the control and treatment used different effective output depths. A matched comparison later reported a 3.20-point offline gain for enabling the interaction head, and a separate seven-day randomized online test reported a 0.66% relative increase in the product’s VDD slice of Good Search Result Rate for Retention. The operational analysis includes nine of twenty rounds with complete records; results are reported by the system’s authors and do not establish cross-organization performance.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: EvoPilot uses human-approved rounds, isolated workers, a versioned domain skill and typed adapter, durable experiment records, artifact-based comparison checks, and human review to admit a control-treatment comparison.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a 37-day Video Deep Dive campaign, the authors found a primitive autoresearch comparison with a reported 22-percentage-point offline hit-rate decline had an effective output-depth mismatch: control K_eff=3000 and treatment K_eff=600, although both declared K=600.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: After correction, a matched-lineage comparison at K=3000 reported a 3.20-percentage-point offline increase when the interaction head was enabled with candidate depth changing from P=3000 to P=6000; the authors state that the head-off control is invariant to P.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A separate seven-day randomized online experiment reported a statistically significant 0.66% relative increase in the Video Deep Dive slice of Good Search Result Rate for Retention; retained guardrail outcomes were unavailable.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The longitudinal campaign inventory contained 20 approved rounds, but only nine had complete operational records; paired replay admitted all ten clean fixtures and blocked all ten corresponding mutated faults.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent replication or implementation of EvoPilot outside the authors’ Meta retrieval deployment was inspected.
The replay tests do not establish how often guards detect real-world invalid comparisons or block valid ones.
Offline uncertainty and online guardrail outcomes are absent from the retained evidence described in the paper.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported evidence controls and corrected comparisons work as described, they could materially improve the reliability of long-running model experiments that cross training, publishing, serving and evaluation systems. The paper is a single company deployment with only nine complete operational rounds and replay-only evidence for some guards, so consequence is meaningful but not yet general.
limitations: The paper is an author-reported case study from one company and retrieval product; it does not establish that EvoPilot generalizes across organizations or experiment systems.
Only 9/20 rounds had complete operational records; 11 were excluded from operation-rate denominators, and the earlier campaign lacks a complete attempt denominator.
The 10 clean and 10 mutated replay fixtures do not establish field recall or false-block rates; some identity controls were added after the study and evaluated only by replay.
Offline confidence intervals, online guardrail outcomes and cross-organization replication are unavailable.
The online GSRR result estimates the selected interaction-head treatment, not the causal effect of EvoPilot.
brief.summary: Meta authors describe EvoPilot, a human-gated agent workflow for experiments spanning asynchronous training, publishing, serving and evaluation systems. In one 37-day Video Deep Dive campaign, an initial autoresearch comparison appeared to show a 22-point offline hit-rate decline, but review found the control and treatment used different effective output depths. A matched comparison later reported a 3.20-point offline gain for enabling the interaction head, and a separate seven-day randomized online test reported a 0.66% relative increase in the product’s VDD slice of Good Search Result Rate for Retention. The operational analysis includes nine of twenty rounds with complete records; results are reported by the system’s authors and do not establish cross-organization performance.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that human-gated verification rejected a false negative caused by a mismatch between declared and effective output depth. A later matched-lineage comparison reported a 3.20-percentage-point offline increase for the head-on treatment at its selected operating point. A separate seven-day randomized test reported a 0.66% relative increase in the VDD slice of GSRR. Replay/mutation tests admitted 10/10 clean fixtures and blocked 10/10 paired faults.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected primary source is a Meta-authored arXiv preprint with a detailed single-product longitudinal study and a separate randomized online experiment. No independent implementation or cross-organization evaluation was inspected. The online 0.66% relative estimate is attributed only to the selected interaction-head treatment, not to EvoPilot itself.
technical.mechanism: A human-approved round protocol specifies the shared base, data pins, metric, required artifacts and authorized contrast. Isolated worker roles execute variants through a versioned domain skill and adapter. A deterministic verifier compares terminal artifacts and realized settings at the pair level; missing evidence or an unauthorized difference blocks admission. Human review retains authority over metric semantics, exceptions and stopping. Durable evidence and incident records carry context between sessions and rounds.
technical.regime: One Meta Video Deep Dive retrieval system backed by an hourly refreshed index of hundreds of millions of videos. The 37-day campaign spanned seven research directions and 20 approved rounds, but only nine rounds had complete operational records. The online experiment covered a seven-day US/Canada VDD-pivot metric slice; it reported a relative effect on GSRR, not percentage-point lift.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the offline interaction-head comparison, control and treatment use the same trained checkpoint and K=3000; the head-off control uses P=3000 while the head-on treatment rescored candidates at P=6000. The paper states that P does not affect the head-off output. Online, the randomized control and treatment kept the remainder of the serving system fixed; accounts were the assignment and analysis unit.

brief.title: Meta paper reports agentic experiment controls caught a false negative in a 37-day retrieval campaign
brief.why_it_matters: The case shows how a completed model experiment can still support a false conclusion when realized evaluation settings differ from their declared values. Pair-level artifact checks, retained failure records and human approval corrected the comparison in this deployment, while the paper also reports limits in its own controls and records. If repeated elsewhere, this protocol could improve long-horizon model experimentation; one company’s case study cannot establish general effectiveness.
